Article and publisher sources.why_it_matters: Prefer first-party research, engineering, official product changes, or highly expert practitioner work.
Material should contain enough technical or operational detail to support accurate Brief coverage.
Strong fit with reliable generative AI, agents, context/RAG, evals, knowledge work, and AI-assisted development.
Regular, substantive publishing without excessive promotional noise.
Reward sources that add missing ecosystems, independent viewpoints, or under-covered technical domains.
Stable URLs, archives, feeds, or reliably searchable pages improve deterministic discovery.

Research and early-signal discovery.why_it_matters: How early the source exposes meaningful research, releases, benchmarks, or implementation patterns.
Primary papers, code, benchmarks, reproducible methods, or clearly scoped measurements score highest.
Prioritize agents, model capabilities, tool use, safety, coding, RAG, evaluation, and infrastructure.
Prefer surfaces where a meaningful change is discoverable without overwhelming unrelated volume.
Balance vendor signals with academic, nonprofit, public-sector, and community evidence.
Stable pages, APIs, feeds, or structured leaderboards are advantageous but not mandatory.

Video discovery.why_it_matters: Official labs, research institutions, engineering communities, and expert educators outrank generic channels.
Prefer demonstrations, talks, workshops, and technical explainers over promotional clips.
Videos should support practical understanding of agents, AI engineering, knowledge work, or major developments.
Recent, recurring content creates a dependable candidate pool.
Channel identity, upload date, runtime, and linked evidence should be checkable.
Shorter useful videos are easier to fit the Brief, while longer talks remain discovery inputs.

Podcast discovery.why_it_matters: Interviews and analysis should add context beyond headline repetition.
Strong relevance to applied generative AI, knowledge work, agents, engineering, enterprise adoption, or major developments.
Reliable publication improves odds of finding worthwhile recent episodes.
Prefer credible builders, researchers, operators, and direct evidence.
Balance technical, enterprise, practitioner, and independent reporting perspectives.
Stable episode catalogs, RSS, Apple/Spotify/YouTube presence, and clear dates improve verification.

Emerging AI Watchlist.why_it_matters: The source should surface meaningful developments before they are broadly established.
Primary sources score highest; aggregators must make it easy to trace to original evidence.
Reward coverage of models, tools, practices, agents, research, open source, and workflow innovation.
High-value leads should be identifiable without excessive duplication or hype.
Daily or frequent publishing improves detection latency.
Avoid overconcentration in one vendor, geography, or evidence type.
Reliable retrieval, stable pages, feeds, or a clear assisted-review path.
